title: Right-derived unit normalization of the canonical open exchange
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, and let b:U→V, q:U→W, p:V→Z and i:W→Z form a cartesian square of schemes, with b and i open immersions. Let I=i!, O=b!, R=q* and P=p* on constant-A module sheaves. Write Q for homotopy localization, f_I and f_O for exact-derived homotopy factor isomorphisms, and u_R,u_P for right-derived units. Let bc:q^*⋙b!≅i!⋙p^* be ordinary open base change, χ:R⋙I→O⋙P the mate of its inverse, and Γ:R(R)⋙D(I)→D(O)⋙R(P) the canonical derived open exchange. For every homotopy object L of sheaves on U, D(I)(u_R(L)) followed by Γ(QL) and R(P)(f_O(L)) equals f_I(RL) followed by Q(χ̄_L) and u_P(OL), where χ̄ includes the canonical homotopy composition isomorphisms. No properness or finiteness assumptions are needed for this forward identity. Conventions: [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

proof.text: For arbitrary exact functors, expand the exact-derived square construction to show that the square of the inverse ordinary isomorphism equals the inverse derived square. Specialize to ordinary open base change.

Apply the mixed derived mate unit normalization with the specified inverse derived base-change square and its symmetry equality. Unfold the canonical open exchange and derived upper-star/lower-star adjunction names to identify the result.
